verdicts.factCheck: build/checksums.txt line 8 reads '# version:golang 1.27.2' at v1.17.9, '1.27.3' at v1.17.10 and '1.27.4' at master (fetched). core/vm/interpreter.go at v1.17.9 runs execTraced only when forceTableLoop, IsEIP4762, ExtraEips or a Tracer is set and execUntraced otherwise (fetched, lines 130-136 of the file as served). The v1.17.10 interpreter_gen.go merges DUP1 to DUP16 and SWAP1 to SWAP16 into two cases that call stack.dup(n) and stack.swap(n); stack.go at v1.17.10 lines 229-240 implement them as copy of the n-th word with size and arena top both incremented, and exchange of the top with top-n, which matches the specification. The release page lists #35638 (inlined switch, v1.17.9) and #35959 (DUP/SWAP dispatch, v1.17.10). Go issue 81863 describes a dead store eliminated after branchelim for a pointer selected between two stack locals, fixed by CL 841425 with backports for 1.27 and 1.26. go.mod at v1.17.9 pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. web3_clientVersion on blockpi returned Geth/v1.17.9-stable-9dffe6e9/linux-amd64/go1.27.2 in 15 of 15 calls. The same call on eth.api.pocket.network returned reth v2.11.0 (19), reth v2.10.1 (8) and erigon 3.8.1 built with go1.27.3 (3) in 30 calls, and erigon 3.8.2 go1.27.2 once more in a separate sample; it never returned geth. Pocket is a load balanced gateway, so the claim that a go1.25.14 geth build was tested there is not reproduced.
verdicts.codeCheck: The cited lines do what the finding says and none depends on a Go compiler shape: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-25 compute prod1 from mulmod(a, b, not(0)), FullMath.sol:48 computes the remainder with mulmod, and src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-27 compress with signextend, sdiv and smod. The finding claims no change in these results; it only names the lines a miscompiled handler would reach. No fund path exists: a miscompile in one client build would be a consensus split between clients, which an ordinary account cannot aim at a pool.
verdicts.corrections: Go issue 81863 also affects go1.26 releases before the 1.26 backport (#81865), not only go1.27.0 to go1.27.3; the bug entered with a July 2025 commit. The 'geth v1.17.9 built with go1.25.14 (pocket)' results in the mechanism, and the conclusion that two toolchains agree on the same source, rest on an endpoint that load balances reth v2.11.0, reth v2.10.1 and erigon 3.8.x; in 30 samples no geth backend answered, so those runs mostly tested reth and erigon, and the go1.25.14 geth build is untested. The blockpi geth v1.17.9 go1.27.2 results stand. Actor operator is acceptable: no party can choose the build that validators run except the operators themselves.

sources.supports: geth v1.17.9 pins go 1.27.2; v1.17.10 pins 1.27.3; master pins 1.27.4.
execUntraced is used unless a tracer, ExtraEips, EIP-4762 or forceTableLoop is set.
Merged DUP and SWAP cases with bounds n and n+1, overflow limit 1023 for DUP, constant gas 3.
Stack.dup(n) and Stack.swap(n) implement DUPn and SWAPn as specified.
branchelim and dead store miscompile, backports opened for 1.26 (#81865) and 1.27 (#81866).
v1.17.9 notes #35638 inlined switch; v1.17.10 notes #35959 DUP/SWAP dispatch.

leads.question: Which public mainnet endpoint pins a single backend for geth v1.17.9 or v1.17.10 built with a toolchain other than go1.27.2, and do battery.py, targeted.py and pushdup.py match there?
leads.why: The go1.25.14 geth runs were served by a load balanced gateway that answered with reth and erigon, so a second geth toolchain has not been tested. erigon 3.8.1 on the same gateway is built with go1.27.3, also inside the Go 81863 range.
